This dataset "WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes.RData" contains all the RAW data for IB and GE before any imputation (after having reversed the corresponding stressors) . It does not have SES covariate because the calculation must be done after imputation.

```{r}

load(file = "../data/WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes.RData")

```




### B) SUBSET for GENE EXPRESSION regressions (SUBSET B):

```{r}
# 1) List of all 11 PRESELECTED stressors (positive associations with IBs) :
stress_all_vars = c("A1PC3", "A1PC14", "A1SE9", "A1SE11", "A1SE14C", "A1SE14D", "A1SE14E", "A1SE14F", "A1SE14G", "A1SE14H", "A1SE14I", "A1SE14J", "A1SE14K", "A1SE15", "A1SE16C", "A1SE16D", "A1SE16E", "A1SE16F", "A1SE16G", "A1SE16H", "A1SE16I", "A1SE16J", "A1SE16K", "A1SE17A", "A1SE17B", "A1SE17C", "A1SE17D", "A1SE17E", "A1SE17F", "A1SE17G", "A1SE17H", "A1SE17I", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17K", "A1SE17L", "A1SE17M", "A1SE17N", "A1SE17O", "C1SJ1", "C1SJ4A", "C1SJ4B", "C1SJ4C", "C1SJ4H", "C1SJ4J", "C1SJ5", "C1SJ8A", "C1SJ8B", "C1SJ8C", "C1SJ8F", "C1SJ8H")


# 3) List the covariates (or common variables) used in all models:
common_vars <- c("MIDUSID", "C1PRSEX", "C1PRAGE", "C1PB1", "C1SBMI", "C1SA26F", "C1STINC", "C1PHHSIZE", "C1SA11T")

# 4) List of CF tasks:
CFs = c("C3TWLITU", "C3TDBS", "C3TCTFLU", "C3TNSTOT", "C3TBKTOT", "C3TSCGBA" , "C3TEM", "C3TEF") #I am using the RAW version of C3TSCGBA for imputation.

# 5) List of GENES:
# Column number of the first gene:
which(names(WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes) == "RA6RCXCL8")
# Get the gene names (51 genes):
  # Extract the names of the columns, excluding the first 126:
all_genes = colnames(WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes)[85:ncol(WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes)]
all_genes 
# 6) List of additional covariates specifically for GE analyses:
covar_ge= c("RA6RPLATE", "RA6RCD3E",  "RA6RCD3D", "RA6RCD4", "RA6RCD8A", "RA6RCD14", "RA6RCD19", "RA6RFCGR3A", "RA6RNCAM1" )


### Group all variables that are going to use in GE regressions and mediations:
all_vars=c(stress_all_vars, common_vars, CFs, all_genes, covar_ge)


###### Subset all requiered variables: 
subset_white_mediations_GE= WHOLE_dataset_white_all_genes[, all_vars]
sum(complete.cases(subset_white_mediations_GE))

library(ggplot2)
library(naniar)
vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_GE, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 50, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))

```

The **complete cases** of this full dataset is only **~300 rows**!!!


###### A) Creating <16% missing - dataset:


I have to still use part of the previous filtering method to get a dataset with <15% missing data.

```{r}
library(naniar)
library(dplyr)

#######  Filter 1:
# Retain individuals with AT LEAST ONE non-missing GE value (it is the same that filter out individuals with all GE=NA values)
subset_white_mediations_GE_2 <- subset_white_mediations_GE %>%
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(subset(., select = all_genes))) >= 1)
vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_GE_2, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 50, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))
dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_2)

```



```{r}
#######  Filter 2:

# Remove individuals with > 5 NA in stressors (retain individuals with at least 45 non-missing values) 
subset_white_mediations_GE_3= subset_white_mediations_GE_2 %>%
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(subset(., select = stress_all_vars))) >= 45)

vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_GE_3, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))

```


```{r}
#######  Filter 3:
# Abuse related variables "17....):
abuse_var= c( "A1SE17E", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17O", "A1SE17I", "A1SE17D", "A1SE17N") 

# Exclude rows where at least 10 of the abuse_var are missing (only retain individuals with valid data in more than 4 of the stressors)
subset_white_mediations_GE_4 = subset_white_mediations_GE_3  %>%
  filter(
    !(rowSums(is.na(subset(., select = abuse_var))) >= 4) # Minimum= 4. less than that, decreseases the % too much
  )

dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_3)
dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_4)
vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_GE_4, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))

```


```{r}
#######  Filter 4:

# NOTE:   The last filter achieve 16%. To remove the other 1% (10 individuals) I will select them randomly from people with NA data in those streassors that have > 16%:
str_5=c("A1SE17E", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17O","A1SE17H", "A1SE17M", "A1SE17C")

# 1. Append a helper column counting NAs across str_5
data_miss <- subset_white_mediations_GE_4 %>%
  mutate(miss_str5 = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(str_5)))))

# 2. Find the row-indices of the top most-missing (ties are broken by order in the data)
rows_to_remove <- head(order(data_miss$miss_str5, decreasing = TRUE), 10)

# 3. Slice those rows out, and drop the helper column
subset_white_mediations_GE_5 <- data_miss %>%
  slice(-rows_to_remove) %>%
  dplyr::select(-miss_str5)

dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_4)    
dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_5)    

vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_GE_5, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))
```

```{r}
#######  Filter 5:

# NOTE:   The last filter achieve 18%. To remove the other 1% (10 individuals) I will select them randomly from people with NA data in those streassors that have > 18%:
str_x= c("A1SE17E", "A1SE17J", "A1SE17O")

# 1. Append a helper column counting NAs across str_5
data_miss <- subset_white_mediations_GE_5 %>%
  mutate(miss_str5 = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(str_x)))))

# 2. Find the row-indices of the top most-missing (ties are broken by order in the data)
rows_to_remove <- head(order(data_miss$miss_str5, decreasing = TRUE), 8)

subset_white_mediations_GE_6 <- data_miss %>%
  slice(-rows_to_remove) %>%
  dplyr::select(-miss_str5)

dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_5)    
dim(subset_white_mediations_GE_6)    

vis_miss(subset_white_mediations_GE_6, sort_miss = TRUE) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 35, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10))


```


```{r}
#######  Filter 6:

# NOTE:   The last filter achieve 18%. To remove the other 5 individuals I will select them randomly from people with NA data in those 2 stressors that have > 18%:
str_x= c("A1SE17E", "A1SE17J")

# 1. Append a helper column counting NAs across str_5
data_miss <- subset_white_mediations_GE_6 %>%

# 2. Find the row-indices of the top-9 most-missing (ties are broken by order in the data)

```


#### - Imputation:


```{r}
### Impute all the variables except by genes (and gene covariates): 

# Group all GE-related variables needed :
all_vars_GE=c(all_genes, covar_ge)

# 1) Exclude genes from the dataset: 
library(dplyr)
subset_white_to_impute_GE= subset_white_mediations_GE_7[ , !(names(subset_white_mediations_GE_7) %in% all_vars_GE)]
str(subset_white_to_impute_GE)

# 2) Split the dataset by sex: 
subset_white_to_impute_GE_M= subset(subset_white_to_impute_GE, C1PRSEX==1)
subset_white_to_impute_GE_F= subset(subset_white_to_impute_GE, C1PRSEX == 2)

nrow(subset_white_to_impute_GE_M)
```


```{r}
###### Impute the data:

### 1) Male group Imputation: 
# Perform multiple imputation:
library(mice)
subset_white_imputed_GE_M <- mice(subset_white_to_impute_GE_M, m = 1, method = 'pmm', maxit = 50, seed = 500)
# Extract the complete dataset:
subset_white_imputed_GE_M_complete <- complete(subset_white_imputed_GE_M)
head(subset_white_imputed_GE_M_complete)

# Visualize the NA data patterns: 
vis_miss(subset_white_imputed_GE_M_complete)


### 2) Female group Imputation: 
subset_white_imputed_GE_F <- mice(subset_white_to_impute_GE_F, m = 1, method = 'pmm', maxit = 50, seed = 500)
# Extract the complete dataset:
subset_white_imputed_GE_F_complete <- complete(subset_white_imputed_GE_F)

# Visualize the NA data patterns: 
vis_miss(subset_white_imputed_GE_F_complete)
```

```{r}
### Re-merge the 2 sex groups:
subset_white_imputed_GE_complete=rbind(subset_white_imputed_GE_F_complete, subset_white_imputed_GE_M_complete)
str(subset_white_imputed_GE_complete)

# Create a dataset with only the GE-related variables: 
all_vars_GEm= c(all_vars_GE, "MIDUSID")
gene_vars_white_df= subset_white_mediations_GE_3[ , (names(subset_white_mediations_GE_3) %in% all_vars_GEm)]
head(gene_vars_white_df)

# Merge the imputed data with the genes:
subset_white_imputed_complete_GE= merge(subset_white_imputed_GE_complete, gene_vars_white_df, by="MIDUSID")
str(subset_white_imputed_complete_GE)
```


```{r}
##### Create the FINAL DATASET for white population using only complete cases: 
complete_cases_white_GE=complete.cases(subset_white_imputed_complete_GE)
sum(complete_cases_white_GE)

# Subset the dataframe to include only complete cases:
subset_white_final_GE = subset_white_imputed_complete_GE[complete_cases_white_GE, ]
str(subset_white_final_GE) # Contains imputed data only for the 20 selected individual stressors
```
FINAL N = 217 (SUBSET B)


```{r}
### Some subset (A) STATS: 

# Age: 
range(subset_white_final_GE$C1PRAGE)
mean(subset_white_final_GE$C1PRAGE)
sd(subset_white_final_GE$C1PRAGE)

# Sex:

(sum(subset_white_final_GE$C1PRSEX == 2) / sum(!is.na(subset_white_final_GE$C1PRSEX))) * 100

```

#### - Creation of SES variable:

```{r}
# Create the SES using the 2 variables that compound it (Education, household income). The other variable (occupational prestige) was not available for these 2 waves and nothing similar was measured in MIDUS. 

# 1) Adjust income for household size: 
subset_white_final_GE= subset_white_final_GE %>% 
  mutate(adjusted_income = C1STINC / C1PHHSIZE)

# 2) Standardize the variables (z-score):
subset_white_final_GE = subset_white_final_GE %>%
  mutate(
    z_education = scale(C1PB1, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE),
    z_income = scale(adjusted_income, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
  )


# 3) Compute SES as the average of the z-scores:
subset_white_final_GE = subset_white_final_GE %>%
  mutate(SES = (z_education + z_income) / 2)


head(subset_white_final_GE[, c("C1PB1", "C1STINC", "C1PHHSIZE", "adjusted_income", "z_education", "z_income", "SES")])

```


#### -  Filter individuals with 3 Diseases: 

I am removing all individuals with history (diagnosed) of: 
- cancer
- Parkinson's disease
- other neurological disorder
 

```{r}

ind_diseases= read.csv("../data/individuals_diseases_few.csv")
```



```{r}
# Remove individuals with IDs listed in ind_diseases$diseases
subset_white_final_GE<- subset_white_final_GE[!subset_white_final_GE$MIDUSID %in% ind_diseases$diseases,]
dim(subset_white_final_GE)

```

Final N = 209 individuals x 131 columns (subset B)

